nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae that make the sea's base food, thriving where upwelling brings nutrients.

nodes.name: Zooxanthellae
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae living inside coral that pass sugars to their host.

nodes.name: Seagrass
nodes.desc: Underwater meadows that shelter young fish and feed turtles and dugongs.

nodes.name: Macroalgae
nodes.desc: Seaweeds on reef flats that grazers keep from smothering the coral.

nodes.name: Reef-building coral
nodes.desc: Builds the limestone reef that shelters thousands of other species. It bleaches when warm water drives out its algae.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny drifting animals that graze phytoplankton and feed fish, manta rays and coral.

nodes.name: Damselfish
nodes.desc: Guards patches of algae and picks plankton from the water above the reef.

nodes.name: Parrotfish
nodes.desc: Scrapes algae off the reef with a beak and excretes the ground limestone as sand.

nodes.name: Surgeonfish
nodes.desc: Grazes algae in schools so seaweed does not overgrow corals.

nodes.name: Green sea turtle
nodes.desc: Grazes seagrass meadows, which keeps them healthy.

nodes.name: Dugong
nodes.desc: A large marine mammal that feeds almost entirely on seagrass.

nodes.name: Crown-of-thorns starfish
nodes.desc: Eats coral polyps. Outbreaks can strip large stretches of reef.

nodes.name: Butterflyfish
nodes.desc: Nips at coral polyps and small invertebrates.

nodes.name: Reef manta ray
nodes.desc: Filters zooplankton from the water with its wide mouth.

nodes.name: Moray eel
nodes.desc: Ambushes fish from crevices in the reef.

nodes.name: Coral trout
nodes.desc: A reef predator that hunts damselfish and parrotfish.

nodes.name: Giant trevally
nodes.desc: Patrols the reef edge, hunting fish in groups.

nodes.name: Giant triton
nodes.desc: A large sea snail that eats crown-of-thorns starfish.

nodes.name: Migratory shorebirds
nodes.desc: Winter visitors that feed on small animals among reef-flat algae and rubble before flying north to breed in the Arctic.

nodes.name: Tiger shark
nodes.desc: Eats turtles, dugongs, fish and carrion, and roams widely over seagrass and reef.

nodes.name: Blacktip reef shark
nodes.desc: Hunts reef fish in shallow water.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Bright, shallow water lets algae live inside coral.

nodes.name: Seawater & currents
nodes.desc: Warm, clear water carries plankton and keeps temperature in the narrow range corals tolerate.

nodes.name: Nutrients
nodes.desc: Upwelling and river runoff supply nitrogen and phosphorus. Too much feeds algae at the coral's expense.

nodes.name: Bacteria & sponges
nodes.desc: Recycle dead matter and dissolved organics and return nutrients to the water.
